mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,600-£3,100 supply-only, depending on power output and supplier. EP6DT 156hp units start around £1,600, while EP6FDT 165hp units range £1,700-£3,100. Used engines start from £700. Supply & fit adds £400-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £4,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle, high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure causing hard starting and misfires, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, and turbocharger oil feed line leaks. The EP6FDT 165hp variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 3008 1.6 THP values typically £3,000-£8,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,600-£3,100 represents a significant investment but often makes sense for well-maintained examples. For sub-£4,000 examples, a used engine from £700 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP (EP6DT/EP6FDT) engine can reach 100,000-130,000 miles. However, HPFP failure can appear as early as 50,000 miles, and timing chain issues from 60,000-90,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil, timely timing chain replacement and HPFP monitoring are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP and 1.2 PureTech engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP (EP6DT/EP6FDT) is a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 156-165hp, while the 1.2 PureTech is a 1.2-litre turbocharged three-cylinder producing 110-130hp. The 1.6 THP uses a timing chain (which can stretch), while the PureTech uses a wet timing belt (which can degrade). The 1.6 THP is more powerful but also more complex and was only available in first-generation 3008s (2009-2016), whereas the PureTech powers second-generation models.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine code is EP6DT (5FN) for 156hp models or EP6FDT (5GK) for 165hp models. It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP (Turbo High Pressure) was the performance petrol option for the first-generation (2009-2016) 3008, bringing turbocharged power to the crossover SUV. Powered by the Prince engine family - jointly developed by PSA and BMW - the 1.6 THP delivered up to 165hp, making it the most powerful petrol engine in the early 3008 range. First introduced in 2009, the 1.6 THP featured twin-scroll turbocharging, direct injection and advanced engine management. However, its complexity and well-documented reliability issues - particularly timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure and carbon buildup - have made it a growing source of replacement enquiries for owners of the 3008 Active, Allure and GT Line.

milestones.description: **2009** - Peugeot 3008 launched with 1.6 THP 156hp (EP6DT, 5FN) for Active, Allure and GT Line trims
**2010** - Minor ECU refinements to improve cold-start behaviour
**2012** - Timing chain tensioner revisions introduced to address early failures
**2013** - Facelift models receive updated HPFP and turbo oil feed lines
**2014** - EP6FDT (5GK) Euro 6 variant introduced for later facelift models
**2016** - First-generation 3008 production ends; 1.6 THP discontinued in favour of PureTech units

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EP6DT, 5FN and EP6FDT engine fitted to the Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP (EP6DT/5FN) is a thrilling engine when running well, but its Prince architecture - shared with BMW and Mini - has well-documented weaknesses. Timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure, carbon buildup and turbocharger issues are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The EP6FDT 165hp variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear. Every rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP Engines Rattle and Fail
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. Peugeot released a TSB with revised tensioner and guide parts.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle, address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6DT/EP6FDT Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP Engines Fail to Start and Run Roughly
problems.rootCause: The Bosch HPFP's internal cam follower wears prematurely, causing metal contamination to circulate through the high-pressure fuel rail and injectors. Symptoms include hard starting, rough idle, misfires and, in severe cases, complete non-start. The EP6FDT 165hp variant is particularly susceptible due to higher fuel pressures. Fault code P0087 (low fuel pressure) is a common indicator.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, flush fuel lines, replace inline filter
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before metal debris reaches injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full rebuild with upgraded HPFP and cleaned rail, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Essential when metallic particles have contaminated the combustion chambers

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP is catastrophic if delayed. If diagnostic codes show fuel rail pressure deviation alongside metallic fuel, budget for a full engine replacement immediately - repairing injectors alone will not prevent repeat failure. The EP6FDT 165hp variant is especially susceptible; HPFP failure is one of the most common reasons for 3008 1.6 THP engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Find specialist Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP rebuilt engines with upgraded HPFP

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Oil Feed Issues - Additional Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger's oil feed line can leak or become restricted, starving the turbo of lubrication and leading to bearing failure. Carbon deposits in the turbo can also cause wastegate sticking. The EP6FDT 165hp variant places additional stress on the turbo system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of turbocharger and oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new turbo and oil feed system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 3008 1.6 THP has turbo lag or blue smoke, have the oil feed lines inspected immediately. Replacing these components early can prevent catastrophic turbo failure. Once turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, a full rebuilt engine is the safest option.
